summary: Hike-in lookout in the Gospel Hump Wilderness: a 1929 cupola cabin replaced by an R-6 cab in 1963. Sources differ on whether it is staffed every season or in summer.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources describe the 1929 cabin as log (NHLR and Forest Service), shake (firelookout.com) or gable-roofed (Forest Lookouts Idaho). All agree it had a cupola and was the first permanent lookout; the wall material cannot be settled from these sources.
NHLR and firelookout.com describe the 1963 cab's base as concrete; Forest Lookouts Idaho describes a cinder-block enclosed storage area. All agree the base is about seven feet high.
NHLR says the lookout is staffed every season and the undated Forest Service post says the 1963 cab remains staffed to this day; firelookout.com says staffed in the summer. The season is not settled.

notes_for_editor: Elevation conflict not resolved and worth a human look: NHLR gives 8,373 ft (2,552 m), which matches the record's elevation_m, but firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts give 8465 ft (about 2,580 m). Distance from Elk City: 24 miles (firelookout.com) vs about 25 miles (Forest Service post). Staffing sources conflict on season: NHLR says every season, firelookout.com says summer, and the undated Forest Service post says staffed to this day. The story no longer says staffing 'has been steady'. Brief's access 'unknown' is now public hike-in per sources. Climbability of the cab is not stated in any source read, so no climbable flag is recorded. No fire involving the lookout was found in the sources. Idaho Fire Lookouts lists a 1929 'Known Staff' entry without a name. height_m 2.1 is the 7-foot base described by sources, used as the cab-floor height proxy.
